# Independent visual review of the extended batch

**APPROVE all three stylesheet changes on index-67e9fa8e.css.** I compared the compiled candidate on port 4252 with index-0731cabb.css on port 4251. I used the editorial hierarchy, typography, black canvas, focus treatment and component roles in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md as the reference.

| Implemented change | Decision | Actual site findings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native text selection on marked Shiki lines | **APPROVE** | On Troubleshooting dsregcmd, the original selected range nearly disappears into the already highlighted line. The revised neutral fill has visibly distinct start and end points. It confines the emphasis to the selected glyph range, while the rest of the marked line keeps its band. In the dark example the browser painted black selected ink on #a8a8a8. TX-02 and the surrounding syntax keep their previous geometry and colors when selection clears. The existing code-color tokens suit both themes. |
| Framework SVG backing | **APPROVE** | In the Linux WebKit dark screenshot, five labeled shapes appeared to float separately in the original rendering. The light paper inside the existing rounded graphic restores the directional paths, including the two arrows to and from the central rectangle. The surrounding page stays pure black. Both builds used the same 611×211 desktop drawing. The bounded asset-specific selector is appropriate for a fixed-ink transparent drawing. |
| Mermaid raw source when the renderer is unavailable | **APPROVE** | On Azure Documentation, the longest raw line extended 229px past a 339px-wide source box on phone. All six sources fit horizontally after the change. The longer source takes more vertical space, but its source text and indentation survive and the full labels can be read in a single column. Tablet and desktop needed no extra lines in the sampled source. With the module available all six real drawings rendered in each theme, width and build and reverted to their original white-space treatment. This selector has a clear boundary between source and drawing. |

I opened the two running sites in Chromium and Linux WebKit at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels in both themes. I inspected the three components and surrounding article layout and made independent browser captures. In Chromium I additionally opened Home, Blog, Search and the phone drawer and rendered the normal-motion graph using local copies of the graph libraries in the test browser. The Home certification table had three rows. The graph used one visible drawing at the larger widths and was suppressed on phone. The Blog listing contained 56 titles. Eight Azure Search options appeared, and the drawer opened and dismissed in both themes on both builds. The mobile Search launcher needed a foreground replay after an initial click during hydration. The replay showed the expected options and subsequent navigation. The diagrams were separately tested with the CDN blocked and with the actual module loaded. No material visual regression was attributable to these three changes. Physical phones and native Safari were outside my review. A clean-page layout observation does not settle the separate repeated-refresh production incident.

## Per-evaluation findings

I inspected the raw trial captures and measurements alongside my site checks. These are my own design dispositions. Each row concerns one distinct question.

| ID | Decision | Visual consideration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 Article title tracking and balancing | **Retain** | The long phone headline already has four readable lines at the existing size. Looser tracking makes the first line fill more of the gutter. Balancing redistributes the words, with 28 phone titles changing line division in the 56-title census and zero fewer lines. The tighter original also keeps “Microsoft Defender XDR” together in the phone example. |
| A2 Prose face and leading | **Retain** | Source Serif 4 differentiates the tutorial paragraphs from the SN Pro navigation. The all-sans paragraph is denser despite its similar bounding box. Raising leading across the article increases page length without resolving any colliding lines. |
| A3 Archive title size | **Retain** | Increasing size by 6% added a wrapped line in six titles on phone, and four additional titles wrapped on tablet. The existing serif title, smaller sans date and separate row rule create an adequate hierarchy. |
| A4 Nested list indent | **Retain** | On the Intune tutorial the existing bullet and hanging label visually mark the instruction nested beneath step six. Reducing the indent recovers little width and moves that bullet closer to the numbered step's text edge. |
| A5 TX-02 table chips and wrapping | **Retain** | The modest neutral chips distinguish literal commands from descriptive text. Removing them weakens that distinction. Prohibiting wrapping would enlarge the panning distance needed for long commands. |
| B1 Breadcrumb and metadata opacity | **Retain** | The current article date and breadcrumb destination have discernible emphasis against the quieter duration and breadcrumb ancestor. Uniform secondary ink flattens those roles. |
| B2 Links on varied surfaces | **Retain** | In the callout the underline remains visible at its current thickness. Thickening it competes with a bold linked phrase. I found no lost link label in the backlink and table comparisons. |
| B3 Graph current/visited colors | **Retain** | The dark graph's current ink and accent stand apart from the fine edge network. The warmer visited-color trial changes an accent without resolving crowded node placement. Node positions differed between simulation runs, so palette and identification are the comparable features. |
| B4 Theme transition | **Retain static** | The one-shot interpolation visibly washes the article out during the switch while text ink switches to its destination. The existing immediate transition prioritizes continuous legibility. |
| B5 Fenced code selection | **Change approved** | The selected text becomes distinguishable inside a highlighted line. The range remains readable in both themes. |
| C1 Short landscape Search | **Retain** | Both header variants leave the selected option available and tappable in the landscape test. Shrinking the input saves 18px on the 844px coarse viewport but does not create a new full result row. The existing taller control remains comfortable at enlarged defaults. |
| C2 Footer and backlink targets | **Retain** | The three sampled phone backlinks already presented 50px-high targets. Forcing all footer links into 44px blocks costs footer space without adding useful separation to those backlinks. |
| C3 Nested contents indentation | **Retain** | The current hierarchy can be followed across the contained disclosure and desktop links. The deeper trial indent shifts the selected link farther from the left text edge and reduces its space on the phone. |
| C4 Reader toolbar in short windows | **Retain sticky** | The static treatment exposes more reading space, but can leave the Search opener offscreen on dismissal. The sticky toolbar keeps the same visible place to find Search and reader mode. |
| C5 Embedded fixed-ink SVG | **Change approved** | Concrete restoration of the arrow directions in Linux WebKit dark mode. |
| D1 Pinning Home labels during keyboard traversal | **Retain** | All ten certification links were reachable and hit-testable when reverse tabbing with the existing release of the pinned label. Adding a reserved 7rem scroll inset did not uncover another link in the examined states. |
| D2 Search backdrop | **Retain** | The current backdrop leaves enough context to recognize the underlying article. Increasing opacity and removing blur made the lower article outlines sharper while the actual result set and active selection stayed the same. In my hydrated comparison the preview contained the same 17,850 characters on both sides. |
| D3 Skip-link position | **Retain** | The corner location is conspicuous on first keyboard focus. Moving the box to the center covered three other toolbar controls in the phone trial instead of two. |
| D4 Explorer scrollbar | **Retain** | A wider, higher-contrast track took another 5px from the tablet rail. The expanded tree grew 168px taller at that width. The baseline thumb allows more room for the labels. |
| D5 Unavailable-diagram source | **Change approved** | Four previously side-scrolling mobile source blocks reflow, including the nested Fault Domain example. |

The three rules fit the current SCSS owners, fonts, surfaces and interaction styles. I found no further evidence-supported material visual change in these twenty comparisons. My local captures and tabulations are under visual-live. The three-change comparison is primary.jpg and the raw trial contact sheets are A.jpg, B.jpg, C.jpg and D.jpg.

# Responsive and accessibility review

**APPROVE** each of B5, C5 and D5 for local stylesheet `index-67e9fa8e.css`, compared with the accepted `index-0731cabb.css`. I found no new material accessibility or responsive regression in these three changes. Light and pure-black page inks, the TX-02 code face and the existing focus indications were preserved.

## Actual browser checks

I opened both served builds in Chromium and Linux WebKit at 390, 900 and 1440px, in light and dark, with reduced motion. I inspected the matched screenshots and took an additional set of embedded-object screenshots. I opened the three changed articles, Home, Blog and Search. The first keyboard stop was Skip to main content. Enter focused main. The archive had all 56 rows. After hydration, Search accepted an Azure query, exposed the arrow-selected option and returned focus to its button in all twelve WebKit build/width/theme cases. The six Chromium candidate cases returned eight results. Reduced motion kept the graph canvas unmounted. A separate normal-motion test rendered one local canvas and one expanded canvas, and Escape restored the global-graph launcher. These checks open and close the graph on a fresh page.

| Change | Finding and decision |
| --- | --- |
| B5 · Selected syntax on a marked line | **APPROVE.** Selecting an actual 32-character range visibly separates it from neighboring marked lines. Its ink and fill were ivory on dark gray in light mode, black on light gray in dark mode. The measured text contrasts exceed 6:1. Keyboard Copy returned the 484-character block on both builds. I compared screenshot pixels for a real selection under emulated forced colors. Before and after, the selected fill used the same system purple on white and cyan on black. Normal syntax and TX-02 return on clearing the selection. |
| C5 · Fixed-ink framework SVG | **APPROVE.** WebKit's dark baseline shows isolated labeled shapes on black. The candidate exposes their black connecting arrows and arrowheads on a paper-colored rectangle. At 390px both object frames measure 355 × 123px and the embedded drawing has the same 12 paths. Both themes and the other widths preserve the surrounding layout. The rule targets this single drawing. The existing empty accessible name remains a separate authored-content issue. |
| D5 · Raw diagram source | **APPROVE.** With the CDN blocked, four of six sources needed lateral panning on the phone baseline. Both Chromium and WebKit now fit all six within 339px. In the second block the box grew from 250px to 340px in height, preserving source order. In actual Firefox 400% zoom at 360 CSS px, the four baseline local overflows were 257, 198, 37 and 80px. All six candidate sources fit. Firefox 200% at 720px also passed. A targeted axe scrollable-region check flagged three phone source regions on my baseline run and zero on the candidate. Keyboard activation of the focused Copy button wrote the exact 154-character authored first diagram source. With the CDN available all six SVGs rendered, fit, and the first opened via keyboard. |

The Shiki selector is limited to fenced-code selection outside forced colors. The SVG rule matches the one dark-theme asset. The fallback rule stops matching once the SVG is present. All three live in the existing stylesheet and introduce no additional keyboard stops or running animations. The checked-in-content display, code payload and existing control geometry survived native zoom and the narrow responsive layout.

## Independent decisions on the twenty questions

I examined the rendered comparisons and browser measurements individually. Implemented candidates received the additional actual-build testing above. A retain decision applies to the accepted baseline for that question.

| Question | Decision and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| A1 · Article titles | Retain current tracking and wrapping. Loosening tracking at a 24px browser default increased even the short phone article's header-to-metadata distance by almost 47px. The baseline keeps the full title readable. |
| A2 · Prose family and leading | Retain Source Serif and current leading. The measured 16.175px phone paragraphs already have 26px lines. The 27px trial adds vertical travel. The serif body remains distinguishable beside the sans navigation. |
| A3 · Blog listing type | Retain the archive size independently of article headings. The +6% candidate adds wraps in six of the 56 phone titles. The 16px baseline scans cleanly alongside its 14px dates. |
| A4 · Nested list indentation | Retain the baseline. Tighter nested indentation gains a few characters while weakening the visible distinction between the outer and inner ordered steps. Enlarged native text still exposes the existing list. |
| A5 · TX-02 in table cells | Retain wrapping and the inline-code fill. Forcing single-line commands increased phone table travel from 236 to 255px. Removing the chip removes a second visual cue for the command while earning no reduction in scroll range. |
| B1 · Breadcrumbs and date | Retain the separate inks. Dark breadcrumbs and reading time already measure 9.14:1 and the published date 15.61:1. Flattening the hierarchy gives up the distinction while reading. |
| B2 · Link underlines | Retain the existing hover/focus styling. In the sampled dark callout, table and backlinks, the hovered text measured 11.69, 12.36 and 13.45:1. A 2px underline added weight without improving legibility in these states. |
| B3 · Graph inks | Retain the current edge and accent palette. Current and visited nodes remain differentiated on the live canvas. Global graph opens, labels remain available, Escape restores focus, and mobile and reduced-motion behavior fit the design system. |
| B4 · Background transition | Reject the animation. Changing the background over 180ms while text ink switches at once produces an intermediate low-contrast title, visible in the midpoint screenshots. The existing instantaneous theme pairing is preferable. |
| B5 · Code selection | Adopt the scoped selection treatment. Both colors and system-color screenshots were checked, as above. |
| C1 · Short-screen search | Retain the existing input and close geometry. At 320 × 256 with a 32px default, the alternative recovers 25px but the 266px selected result still requires scrolling in either layout. The start of the keyboard-selected card stays visible. Neither layout can display its full contents at once. |
| C2 · Backlink and footer targets | Retain the present target sizes. Existing phone backlink rows hit at their centers and wrap to 50px where needed. At extreme text size the two sampled footer links already present a 44px-high target. |
| C3 · Contents indentation | Retain current indentation. The phone link landed on the same visible heading in both variants. The target started about 70px below the top at the ordinary phone size. Wider indentation adds pressure on wrapped labels. |
| C4 · Reader toolbar | Retain sticky placement. In the enlarged 844 × 390 case and in the shortest case the static-toolbar trial loses the visible hit target after Search closes. The baseline allows immediate access to the returned control. |
| C5 · SVG canvas | Adopt the card-specific dark backing. WebKit restores directional information without moving the diagram or changing page black. |
| D1 · Keyboard table scrolling | Retain temporary unpinning while a link has focus. Reverse traversal exposed all ten link centers in the tested phone table. Keeping the label sticky introduces a dependence on a hard-coded 7rem reserved width. |
| D2 · Search overlay | Retain the existing 75% tint and 2px blur. Both overlays preserved eight options and the visible selected result. The stronger overlay without blur did not provide a demonstrated focus or readability benefit. |
| D3 · Skip placement | Retain the leading corner. The skip link was the first keyboard stop, outlined, 44px tall and reached main. Centering it overlapped three underlying phone controls while the baseline overlapped two. |
| D4 · Explorer scrollbar | Retain native touch treatment and the existing fine-pointer scrollbar. The wider trial reduced tablet tree width from 167 to 162px and increased scroll height from 5186 to 5354px. Neither recoloring nor extra wrapping provided an access benefit. |
| D5 · CDN-failure source | Adopt soft wrapping on raw text. The real four-way Firefox overflow fell to zero. Focus, copying and loaded diagrams passed. |

Native Windows forced colors, physical phones and assistive-technology speech were outside my test matrix. The older diagram rerender error after a breakpoint crossing and the separately reported live-site refresh behavior require runtime investigation. This review covers the three local stylesheet changes. Raw independent measurements, forced-color pixels, native zoom and keyboard checks are in `/tmp/quartz-extended/access-independent/`.

# Independent CSS and Quartz V5 review of index-67e9fa8e.css

**APPROVE** the three implemented changes individually. **REVISE** before closing the full batch. The separate first-focus defect on the footer remains material on this candidate. Its authoring, keyboard and performance implications need a fresh implementation check.

## Browser and implementation checks

I rendered the accepted build on 4251 and the candidate on 4252 in Chromium and Linux WebKit at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels in light and pure-black dark. Each matrix included Home, Blog, the dsregcmd article, the framework introduction, the Azure Documentation article and the Device Control article. I inspected the paired captures and the affected surrounding text, navigation, controls and page widths. In settled Chromium sessions I also opened Search, selected a result by keyboard, opened and dismissed the graph on larger widths and opened the phone drawer. Search produced eight results. A few unsynchronized first visits missed the Search click before the launcher hydrated. The separate hydrated walkthrough passed. Local reduced-motion pages suppressed the graph. In ordinary motion it rendered at tablet and desktop widths and returned keyboard focus on closing the global view.

The compiled stylesheet changed in three places. A single dark owner rule matches the existing SVG object's data filename. A descendant test limits raw-source wrapping to Mermaid code currently without SVG. A non-forced-color media query changes selection on non-Mermaid preformatted code and its syntax descendants. The native forced-color ink/fill remained identical in my Chromium before/after test. No new script, selector for unrelated UI, runtime dependency or font entered these rules. Source Serif 4, SN Pro and TX-02 retain their design-system roles, and the main dark canvas retains black. Build emitted 913 artifacts, 164 tests passed and the SCSS formatter passed. The general type checker reports the existing two dependency diagnostics.

## Per-evaluation findings

| Question | CSS decision and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| A1 · Long and short article titles | Retain current tracking and wrap. In the 56-article measurements balancing changed the breaks on 28 phone titles without reducing any title height. It splits the Defender product name. Loosening tracking also adds a line to the enlarged short title. |
| A2 · Dense prose | Retain Source Serif 4 and its existing leading. At the same font size SN Pro changes the column's word fit and blurs its distinction from navigation. Added leading consumes vertical reading space without addressing a demonstrated collision. |
| A3 · Archive headings | Retain the smaller archive scale. The 6% increase adds wraps on phone. Existing date and title columns remain distinct when enlarged. The listing and article answer different reading tasks. |
| A4 · Nested instructions | Retain the stronger nesting indent. The tighter trial buys little width and reduces distinction between procedural steps and their substeps. No missing marker in the narrow cases. |
| A5 · TX-02 command cells | Retain wrap opportunities and the chip. Disallowing wraps moves more literal content beyond the local viewport. Removing the background and inset makes command boundaries less clear. |
| B1 · Header metadata | Retain separate date and secondary ink. The ordinary secondary text already contrasts 6.26:1 on ivory and 9.14:1 on black. A uniform ink removes part of that hierarchy. |
| B2 · Links on different surfaces | Retain contextual underline and focus treatment. Applying an equally strong 2px underline across each surface makes dense table cells and related-page links visually heavy. Existing callout links are distinguishable. |
| B3 · Graph colors | Retain the existing edge and role palette. The accent change improves separation of one node pairing but weakens the ordinary/visited pairing on dark and the visited-to-surface contrast. Zoom and hover remain important for the live canvas. |
| B4 · Background animation | Reject the one-shot theme fade. The midpoint in the captured dark/light switch temporarily puts the title near the same tone as the page. The existing instant surface change works with reduced motion. |
| B5 · Native code selection | **APPROVE**. Inverse ink clearly separates the selected region from Shiki's authored marked line. Both code and child-token pseudo-elements obtain the same intended colors in the two engines. The normal text and mono face resume when selection clears. |
| C1 · Short landscape Search | Retain existing controls. Compressing the short panel saves some height but still cannot show a whole result at the largest combined setting. The baseline keeps the selected title reachable, with more room around controls. |
| C2 · Backlinks and footer | Retain the existing spacing. Increasing all row targets adds height without addressing the defect. **REVISE the first keyboard visit**. On both builds and in both engines, pressing Tab from the final sticky backlink focused the Quartz footer link at y=2404 in a 900px viewport. It remained there after 1.4 seconds in light and dark. The visible-image sizing trial warrants a scoped candidate. |
| C3 · Nested contents | Retain the current indentation. The compact alternative offers little practical improvement on desktop, and removes part of the first/second-level distinction on narrow layouts. The disclosure provides useful access on phones. |
| C4 · Reader controls | Retain the sticky controls. The static alternative in a short view places the reader control offscreen after Search dismissal. The existing toolbar reserves predictable access independent of article length. |
| C5 · Framework SVG | **APPROVE**. My WebKit dark comparison showed unconnected colored boxes on black before, and visible black connectors on ivory afterward. The five connectors define the drawing. Chromium already supplied white behind the interior. This rule leaves the other embedded SVG and the page's black reading surface alone. |
| D1 · Focus below pinned table labels | Retain current focus-state unpinning. Both trials reached all ten Home links on reverse traversal. The 7rem scroll-padding alternative depends on a fixed header width and provides no measured improvement. |
| D2 · Search backdrop | Retain 75% surface and 2px blur. The stronger overlay flattens the surroundings without adding results or improving the selected result. Compare hydrated states because preview content arrives asynchronously. |
| D3 · First skip link | Retain the starting-edge placement. It is visibly focused and usable. Centering moves it over an additional mobile toolbar control. |
| D4 · Scrollbar styling | Retain the thin rail scrollbar for fine pointers. The wider trial removes 5px of tablet tree width, adding wrapped labels. The phone already delegates the control to the browser. |
| D5 · Unavailable diagram library | **APPROVE**. Long raw lines in the narrow Azure example used 568px inside 339px before. Candidate source fits that inner width while adding height. All six Markdown payloads remained available and the updated selector ceases to match when the SVG exists. |

The new style does not resolve the already-reported runtime loss of the original Mermaid drawing on a graph visibility change. The user-reported reload defects are separate runtime investigations. A CSS-only review of these three selectors cannot establish either reload fix. I recommend the director hold full convergence pending the material C2 fix. Measurements and screenshots are in the adjacent css-live directory and the paired browser capture folders.

# Independent visual reassessment of index-4fad1124.css

**REVISE the footer focus correction. APPROVE Shiki selection, the WebKit diagram substrate and raw Mermaid source wrapping.** The focused-footer treatment repairs desktop Chromium but introduces an offscreen focused footer link in Linux WebKit on tablet.

I compared the actual served sites on ports 4251 and 4253 against the design system, matching light and pure-black dark themes and 390, 900 and 1440px viewports. The focal test used the article Using Device Control to Block USB Devices in MDE with all 18 source images decoded. I placed focus on the last backlink, pressed Tab twice, Shift+Tab twice, then Tab again. Each step recorded the actual focused element, geometry, viewport, hit-test result and computed image rendering. The scope also included real Home, Blog, Search, the shell example in Troubleshooting dsregcmd, the Framework SVG and the Azure Mermaid fallback. Initial navigation timing required additional replays on some parallel page checks. The independent component captures cover all three dimensions in both themes.

On 1440px Chromium the first Quartz footer link sat at y=2404 in a 900px viewport in the previous build and at y=848 in the candidate. Both candidate footer links and the return to the backlink worked. On the 900px Linux WebKit layout, in both themes, the previous build showed the footer at y=858 on the first real Tab. The candidate moved the focused footer to y=1786. The second Tab recovered to y=858, but Shift+Tab back to the last backlink and another Tab reproduced the same failure. The verified regression is material to keyboard users. Changing image heights only while the footer has keyboard focus can shift the layout again as focus crosses its boundary.

In an independent browser trial I applied a static content-visibility override only to Markdown images with missing or auto intrinsic dimensions. Linux WebKit then kept the tablet backlink at y=789 and Quartz and LinkedIn at y=858 in both directions. The same static trial kept desktop Chromium’s focused links visible. The selector belongs with the existing image rendering rule. Rebuild and obtain fresh reviews of that variant. The full-page article must retain its black and ivory canvases; the correction does not require different theme inks or type.

The earlier three component decisions still hold. The code selection is clearly separated from the Shiki highlighted row. The article diagram recovers its five connectors on black in Linux WebKit. The narrow Mermaid fallback fits horizontally and remains selectable. The source modifications are confined to custom.scss, with the focus-time selector causing the one new defect above. Convergence is pending the corrected implementation and review.

# Fresh independent responsive and accessibility assessments

I compared the accepted :4251 build, the initial selection/SVG/fallback candidate on :4252, the focus-dependent image rule on :4253 and the persistent unsized-image rule on :4254. Both Chromium and Linux WebKit ran the Device Control article at 390, 900 and 1440px, light and black, with reduced motion. Each state ran twice, once using native image loading and once after all article screenshots decoded. I keyboard-focused the last Backlink, pressed Tab to Quartz in the footer, Shift+Tab to the Backlink and Tab forward again. I checked the focused element, its rectangle and the element physically under its center after the page settled.

## First correction, :4253, index-4fad1124.css

| Change | Independent decision |
| --- | --- |
| Selected code in Shiki | **APPROVE.** The actual selected text remains distinct within a highlighted line, both normal themes continue using TX-02, and our forced-color screenshot comparison preserves the platform selection fill. |
| Transparent framework SVG | **APPROVE.** Both light and black WebKit frames preserve the shapes, arrowheads and lines. The image has stable dimensions. |
| Raw Mermaid source | **APPROVE.** The narrow fallback fits its code box. The original diagram source is preserved and keyboard Copy works. |
| Showing screenshots when footer owns focus | **REVISE. Material.** At 900×900 in WebKit the Backlink was focused at y=1717 and the footer link at y=1786. Reversing and repeating gave the same offscreen positions. Native and decoded runs showed this in both themes. Temporarily changing the intrinsic layout as focus arrives cannot reliably provide the geometry the browser needs for its initial scroll. |

Combined decision **REVISE**. I also found an independent desktop WebKit issue. The Backlinks list can be 0px tall in the right rail, leaving a correctly focused anchor fully clipped. It also occurs on :4251.

## Second correction, :4254, index-4755a9aa.css

| Change | Independent decision |
| --- | --- |
| Selected Shiki text | **APPROVE.** The selected code kept the inverse treatment while system selection remained purple on light and cyan on black. Keyboard Copy returned the 484-character sample. |
| Transparent SVG | **APPROVE.** The named framework diagram retains a light backing on black and now shows the relationship between its nodes in WebKit. Its 390px-wide viewport displayed a 355×123px object on both builds. |
| Long fallback source | **APPROVE.** At native Firefox 400% zoom the six raw sources fit locally. A normal Chromium CDN load rendered six SVGs, keyboard Copy produced the 154-character source, and Enter opened the first drawing. |
| Persistent geometry for unsized images | **APPROVE.** On :4254 the actual footer link passed both forward center hit tests in every native/decoded, engine, width and theme combination. The tablet WebKit sequence now lands at y=858 in the footer and y=789 on the reverse Backlink. Both points hit the link. |

**Further correction required for convergence.** At 1440×900 in WebKit the last desktop Backlink has a real 248×50px border box and focus outline, but its scrolling parent measures 248×0px. Its center hits the sidebar rather than the anchor. Slightly below the anchor's top the hit goes to the Backlinks heading. The builds on :4251, :4253 and :4254 all reproduce this in the independent desktop replay. Both directions into the new footer pass. A separate flex-sizing change is needed for the desktop scrolling list.

**Cost and scope.** On :4254 all 18 Device Control article images match the persistent rule. The same-page load still retrieves 18 image resources, and the explicit dimensions on all five IACS images retain Quartz’s automatic skipped-content behavior. The candidate registered no running animation and no additional layouts or style recalculations during my 500ms idle sample. Removing skipped-content optimization can increase offscreen layout work on long articles; this sample does not measure device battery life. The rules remain in custom.scss. Existing type roles and dark surfaces remain consistent across the viewport matrix. A 2px keyboard outline remains visible on the surviving Copy control.

Evidence is in `/tmp/quartz-extended/access-independent/`, including the `footer-*.json` traversal matrices, `desktop.json` with clip ancestors and hit targets, `quiet.json`, the four engine/build component result sets, native Firefox zoom and `final-review.jpg`. Physical screen readers and mobile hardware were outside these checks.

# Independent CSS and Quartz V5 reassessment of index-4fad1124.css

**REVISE the batch.** **APPROVE** Shiki selection, dark framework SVG and raw Mermaid wrapping. **REVISE** the footer condition. The new focus-dependent rule fixes the desktop case but introduces an offscreen keyboard target on the tablet layout.

I compared the compiled initial and revised assets. Their sole difference is one rule setting image content visibility while a footer descendant visibly owns focus. Styles remain in custom.scss. The change introduces no JavaScript or dependency, and its ordinary unfocused state keeps image skipping enabled. The conditional rule changes the intrinsic heights used by the browser during the same focus transition that triggers scrolling. The inconsistency can be observed in both directions.

| Viewport | Browser result |
| --- | --- |
| 390px, light and black | Both Chromium and WebKit revealed the focused footer links, with their top at about 846px in the 900px viewport. Their rendered image style returned to auto on leaving the footer. |
| 1440px, light and black | The previously offscreen first desktop footer target now appears at 848–849px. Reverse focus to the sticky right rail also returned to a visible position. |
| 900px, light and black | On :4253, Chromium reverse Tab moved the focused backlink to y=1729. In Linux WebKit, the focused backlink remained at y=1717 after 1.45 seconds and the next Tab left the footer at y=1786. Center-point hit testing failed for both targets. In the matched baseline the reverse backlink and second forward footer remained visible at y=789 and y=858. The first baseline forward move itself was intermittent. |

In separate WebKit trials I kept intrinsic image sizing stable while both the backlinks and footer owned keyboard focus, enabled image layout permanently, or enabled it only on images whose declared width or height is auto or missing. All three approaches passed the specific 900px three-step forward/reverse/reentry check in both themes. The standing intrinsic-size rule deserves comparison for cold keyboard entry from other controls. Its performance cost should be measured on image-heavy pages. This is a material keyboard accessibility regression in the present candidate.

The three earlier improvements remained independently verifiable. The neutral selection colors still distinguish Shiki source from selected text on an authored highlighted line. Normal and forced palettes keep their separate behavior. WebKit gives the transparent diagram an ivory ground in dark mode, exposing its black connectors. The narrow blocked-module fallback uses normal soft wrapping with its authored line breaks and TX-02 intact. The other chart and the ordinary code boxes retain their own layout. The 390, 900 and 1440px capture pairs include both themes on Chromium and WebKit. The hydrated Chromium Home/Blog, Search, mobile drawer, graph and article checks passed across the two themes. The production build emitted 913 files, all 164 tests and the scoped formatter passed. Search hydration and the already documented runtime reload issues are separate from this CSS defect.

Direct runs and the baseline comparison are recorded in css-live/focus-chromium.json, css-live/focus-webkit.json, css-live/reverse-webkit.json, css-live/trial-reverse-webkit.json, css-live/live-4253.json and the per-engine measurements. ## Other components

- **Fenced code selection.** The neutral selection remains distinct from authored highlighted lines in both themes. The candidate keeps TX-02 and the previous scoped forced-colors behavior.
- **Transparent framework diagram.** Dark WebKit now shows the connecting lines on the ivory diagram canvas. Chromium supplies its own light drawing interior. Other article and page surfaces use the established palette.
- **Raw Mermaid.** On the blocked-library article, soft wrapping exposes the tail of long source lines. The CSS limits this behavior to raw source before an SVG exists. Narrow and wide code regions remain within the page.
- **Keyboard focus on articles with unsized images.** The static image rule keeps the first desktop footer visit and tablet reverse path stable once the image dimensions are available. A fresh WebKit 900px forward/reverse/reentry sequence in both themes hit each intended target. On a cold visit the browser can still learn an image aspect ratio after scrolling. I previously measured the initially visible focused link moving from y848 to y1172 after the last unsized image loaded. Known dimensions in the content are needed to eliminate this residual shift.

The review covers compiled styles and actual browser behavior. The reported duplicated graph canvases and intermittent Home table symptoms are separate reload investigations. CSS sizing and a passing table layout check do not establish a fix for either runtime condition. The project-wide TypeScript check has the two previously recorded dependency errors. The production build, 164 automated tests and scoped stylesheet format check passed.


Detailed measurements are in css-live/percent-final-chromium.json, percent-final-webkit.json, focus-settled-chromium.json and percent-collapsed-webkit.json. The earlier failed auto-basis cases are in long-webkit-4255.json. The 4256 source, selection and SVG capture sets for both engines and reverse-4256-webkit.json provide the surrounding component checks. One WebKit process stopped after collecting 36 of its 40 states. I reran the exact four missing dark 900px states in the same build and checked all 40 distinct rows.

# Independent Design Director decision · November 22, 2026

**APPROVE the five local styling changes in `index-28d2150b.css`. Close the current visual optimization series.** All three independent final reviewers approved this exact stylesheet. My live before-and-after inspection confirmed the failures that required two revisions and the final behavior that resolves them. I found no remaining material regression attributable to the candidate. Production reload behavior and delayed image geometry remain open issues with identified causes.

## Gate and history

I checked the design system, decision log, backlog, progress record, prior four series and four new groups of observations. The series contain 10 initial, 16 continuous, three typography and 20 publication/navigation evaluations. The historical evidence audit lists 49 entries and 118 linked artifacts. Early rejected trial captures are incomplete. The new 20 numbered evaluations, 21 through 40 in the publication/navigation series, each contain a distinct comparison. The total is 69 design evaluations. Five resulting CSS changes went through the implementation gate. The audit count measures design evaluations, including those that retained the current design. I decoded the 28 WebP boards in the new archive and inspected screenshots of the five implemented changes alongside my own browser captures.

| Evaluations | Director disposition |
| --- | --- |
| 21–25 | Keep the existing title, prose, archive, list and inline code styles. Alternative title spacing brought no measurable layout improvement. Enlarging archive headlines raised phone wraps from 21 to 27. Nonwrapping code increased scrolling with doubled type. |
| 26–29 | Keep the hierarchy of secondary ink, link underline treatments, graph colors and immediate theme changes. The trial background transition briefly dropped heading contrast close to 1:1. |
| 30 | Approve native selection colors on fenced code in normal palettes. |
| 31–34 | Keep the present search header, target spacing, Contents indentation and sticky toolbar. Approve the separately verified keyboard corrections in evaluation 32. |
| 35 | Approve the localized backing for the authored framework SVG. |
| 36–39 | Keep the table keyboard treatment, search overlay, leading skip link and Explorer scrollbar. All ten table targets remained reachable. The wider scrollbar reduced usable tree width and increased its height. |
| 40 | Approve wrapping raw Mermaid until its SVG is available. |

## Decision by candidate

| Compiled build | Decision and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 0731cabb | Previous accepted baseline. Comparison images and CSSOM establish the visual and runtime reference. |
| 67e9fa8e | Retain the three component improvements. **REVISE** the batch for the independently reproduced footer keyboard failure. |
| 4fad1124 | **REJECT** the focus-dependent image reflow. On a decoded Device Control page at 900px width my WebKit instance showed first footer focus at y858, then placed the previous backlink at y1717 and repeated footer focus at y1786 in a 900px-tall viewport. |
| 4755a9aa | **APPROVE** steady sizing of article images with missing or automatic dimensions. **REVISE** the batch for the WebKit right-column collapse when expanded Contents shares space with Backlinks. |
| 0d183d32 | **REJECT** using each section’s intrinsic size as its initial flex basis. In both of my engines, with a live graph at 1440×513, the longer list took 136px and the single-link viewport measured 0px. The last Tab stop failed its hit test. |
| 28d2150b | **APPROVE** all five components following fresh independent reviews. The revised 50% basis and existing intrinsic maximum keep the short list visible while giving surplus height to the longer list. |
| Conditional scroll-anchor trial, scratch only | **REJECT**. Under delayed image responses the footer stayed in place, but scrolling back into the article with keyboard focus still on the footer caused a 359.375px reading-position jump in each engine. The existing anchor moved less than 1px. Supplying intrinsic image dimensions addresses the missing geometry at its source. |

## Independent browser inspection

I opened Home, the Active Directory project with sixteen Contents links and one Backlink, the Device Control article, the framework diagram, the Azure documentation article with six raw Mermaid samples and the dsregcmd code example. I compared served stylesheet identities and exercised normal-motion Chromium and Linux WebKit with the graph's actual D3 and Pixi libraries. My 24 observations and captured screenshots are in the director evidence directory. I examined the matched component and surrounding page images as well as measured rectangles and native input. The final reviewers separately covered both themes at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, reduced motion, the second rail shape, native font settings, zoom and forced colors.

- **Contents and Backlinks.** At 1440×513 in both engines, the 16-entry TOC kept 98px for 520px of content. The short list occupied 29px and entirely exposed its 29px link. All 17 sequential Tab stops passed center hit tests. At 1440×512 the whole-rail fallback remained operable. The visual report also verified the fragment destination, collapsed TOC and 102 keyboard focus stops. The CSS reviewer covered 80 expanded and eight collapsed combinations. Earlier measurements of a link rectangle alone were insufficient to establish visibility inside its clipping ancestor.
- **Footer navigation.** Following normal smooth scrolling and full image decode at 900px, the final page repeatedly reached the footer, preceding backlink and footer. The centers were hit-testable. In WebKit these were y858, y789 and y858 at their upper edges. Chromium yielded y857, y789 and y857. This resolves the focused-footer/reverse-navigation conflict. Final accessibility tests include 24 decoded and native-load sequences across both themes and all three widths. A cold image with unknown intrinsic height can still shift a reader or focused footer when the browser learns its aspect ratio.
- **Code selection.** I selected a real 32-character range already on a highlighted dsregcmd line. The inverse range was visibly distinguishable from the pale authored line. In light mode its ink and fill computed to existing theme colors. TX-02 remained the actual CSS family. The forced-colors media guard leaves system range colors in effect.
- **Embedded diagram.** The transparent SVG had invisible dark connectors on the old WebKit canvas. Its boxes and connections are now legible against the existing ivory surface at the same 611px tablet width. The article, navigation and graph retain the black theme. The exact asset selector constrains the rule.
- **Raw Mermaid.** Blocking the rendering module exposed the original source on a 390px phone. Four of six code regions exceeded their available width before the change, by up to 241px in my desktop-scrollbar harness. All six had zero horizontal overrun after the change. The independent full-corpus replay found all ten diagrams on five pages across six theme/viewport cases rendered correctly with Mermaid available. Repeating the same 60 diagram observations with the renderer unavailable produced complete source. Copy and diagram expansion passed the reviewers' functional tests.
- **Home table.** My phone preview scrolled to its measured 430px endpoint in each engine and kept all three rows and ten links. The table remained a labeled keyboard-focusable region. This result complements the real-device-brand production reload investigation described below.

## Implementation, automation and performance

The sole implementation file is `quartz/styles/custom.scss`. Its scoped selectors preserve TX-02, a true-black page, current navigation styles, existing graph behavior and system colors. The CSSOM changed from 604 to 609 style rules. The main CSS grew by 573 bytes uncompressed. No scripts, generated metadata, font resources, dependencies or indexing changes were introduced. The output comparison matched 252 HTML routes’ titles, metadata and canonicals, all 22 scripts and all 13 font resources. The search index retained 160 entries.

The production build emitted 913 files. All 164 unit tests, scoped formatting and whitespace checks passed. The final browser census found no page-level horizontal overflow on 161 routes at each of 320, 801 and 1200px. Actual Google Chrome and Brave each passed ten final theme, viewport and native font settings combinations. Firefox supplied native 200% and 400% zoom and the published cross-browser records include font preference checks. The final 28-sample comparison took seven alternating cold samples per route per build. Median local LCP was 144→124ms on Home and 132→140ms on Device Control. Median CLS was unchanged on both pages (0.0580 and 0.0275), as were font bytes. These observations support a lack of material regression in the measured conditions. They do not characterize field performance.

The separate repository-wide TypeScript check still reports the two baseline dependency declaration failures for micromorph and remark-parse/lib. This site’s Pages workflow builds the site. The type-check workflows are conditional on the upstream Quartz repository. Native macOS/iOS Safari, mobile hardware and screen-reader speech were outside this environment's direct coverage.

## Production findings and disposition

The public graph can mount two canvases after an ordinary warm reload in Google Chrome and Brave. The router's navigation render and the library-ready initial render both progress past asynchronous initialization. The obsolete renderer can still append its canvas. The traced fix prevented stale attachment in an isolated runtime prototype. The production plugin issue remains open.

The Home certification table survived 36 production states with three rows and ten links. All 24 rapid double-reload trials reset its inner horizontal position and then scrolled the full range. A separate 14-load timing check found a transient right fade, lasting up to 172ms in Chrome and 83ms in Brave. All sampled end masks cleared. The published evidence does not reproduce persistent missing rows or permanent loss of scrolling. The relative contribution of duplicate rendering to the delay remains unproven.

The cold-image shift needs real source dimensions. The graph race needs renderer lifecycle work. The table's reload-position behavior needs its own explicit persistence decision if restoration is desired. These findings provide no further justified CSS patch in this batch. A new reproducible styling regression would reopen the review.

**Signed by the independent Design Director. Final disposition: APPROVE the local stylesheet and close the 20-evaluation series.** The change has three completed approvals from Visual Design, Responsive and Accessibility, and CSS and Quartz V5 reviewers in the corresponding final percent reports.
